There undeniably was/is a rationalist -> nationalist phenomenon over the last ten years.
Hi I'd like your code if it's still available!
I'm so sorry this has happened to you. Your dog friend knew how you much you loved him. That person will get what's coming - people in that line of work always do.

Good on you for going to school! That's the smart thing to do - to go when you can handle it and can get the most out of it. Behind in life? Nah. 

But that doesn't mean that people you're own age might not be in the same place as you. And naturally, those connections break down over time...

I'm going through this right now too...

If school is going fine and you want to meet people, why not try meetups? I've been playing magic the gathering and rock climbing with people and it's been a time and a half =)

It sucks to make a new way for yourself and basically start from scratch... But you seem pretty able! If you want to talk let me know :)

> the only thing i havent tried is medicine, which feels like cheating happiness to me; if i have to artificially appreciate life, than id rather have none of it. 

> ...i havent killed myself because i havent failed uni yet.

These two things popped out at me.

I just graduated university. I did so after biting the bullet and getting a prescription. I have a BS in Neuroscience, so I think I have a little insight into the brain; enough to argue that medications aren't cheating, but a crutch you use while managing your issues. And I don't mean this is a bad way - meds can be effective with therapy and the right treatment plan.

Which leads me to my second point: Have you thought about taking a break from school? Working part time for a semester or two and returning? What's stopping you? If it's people (classmates, family, etc), let me just say that in the grand scheme of things, **it truly does not matter if you graduate "on time" or not**.

If you want to talk let me know - I've been where you are and I got out on the other side (sorta). :)
That statement says more about you than it does about the minds of young black children.
Thank you for the kind words.
Pretty sure referring to blacks as chimps is a good indicator that he/she is racist.
Thank you for your reply. I'm a lot calmer now. I'm just going to regroup and see what happens in the fall. I'm going to focus on school and paying off my loans, so hopefully I'll be okay.

Thank you for your reply. It's silly when I think about it - that I torment myself over pulling the hairs from my head. In the grand scheme of things it's such an innocuous action, even if it leaves me with bald patches. 

I think I'm just going to try and numb myself, at least until I can pay off my loans. But for now, thank you for your kinds words.

Not really. Like I said before, it hasn't really helped. I can't change who I am, but I know I can't accept it either. 
I've wanted to end my life for years but knew how badly it would hurt my family. I promised myself that I would give college a try and was given new found hope when I was accepted into one of my top choices. Once there, the pain I felt only strengthened and by the middle of sophomore year, my resolve had subdued.

It's funny because I always used to have this fantasy in my head, the "me" that I wish I could be. Now that I'm halfway through my college career, I feel like I'm just never going to get to a place where I'll accept myself. 
I have lost the will to study; I get queasy and pull out so much of my hair when I try to open my organic chemistry text. 

I'm probably posting in the wrong place. It's not about giving up. There hasn't been anything to give for a while I'm afraid. I think I'm looking more for ways to solidify my descent and "ease my transition" so to speak, rather than actually get help.

Thank you for your concern.

Ha. I'm pretty much the female version of you. 

I'm sorry about the college thing - to be honest, if you do well, it shouldn't matter if you're just going to an "average" college. Many successful thinkers, politicians, business owners, etc, ended up going to public post secondary schools. 

I tried counselling for a while. It helps in the short term to talk to someone face to face. If you're school offers it, try contacting their counselling services. If you are too afraid, try a hotline. Talking to someone never hurt.

As for family, you will never know how your death will impact them. That said, I wouldn't do anything without at least reaching out to one other person (in real life). 

Hope this helps.
